Table of Nations
TAY-buhl uhv NAY-shuhnz
proper noun
The genealogy of Genesis 10, listing the nations descended from the sons of Noah—Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

See also: Table of Nations

📖 Biblical Definition

The Table of Nations is the genealogy of Genesis 10, which traces the families of the sons of Noah—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—and the nations that sprang from them and were divided over the earth after the flood. It is the Bible’s account of the origin of the peoples: by these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands, every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations; and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood. The chapter stands before the account of Babel, which explains the dividing of the one human speech into many; together they teach that all the nations of the earth descend from one family, one ark, one father in Noah, and beyond him from the one man Adam. Paul declared this very truth at Athens: God hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed and the bounds of their habitation. Moses sang that the Most High, when He divided to the nations their inheritance, set the bounds of the people. The dictionary reads the Table of Nations as the charter of the unity and the divine ordering of mankind: all peoples one in blood, descended from Noah and from Adam, scattered and bounded by the providence of God, and destined to be gathered from every nation into the one redeemed people of Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The genealogy of Genesis 10; the nations descended from Noah’s sons—teaching that all peoples are one blood, ordered and bounded by the providence of God.

TABLE OF NATIONS, the genealogy of Genesis 10.

Traces the families of Shem, Ham, and Japheth, Noah’s sons.

The nations divided in the earth after the flood, each after its tongue.

All peoples descend from one ark, one Noah, one Adam.

God made of one blood all nations and set the bounds of their habitation.

📖 Key Scripture

Gen 10:32 — "These are the families of the sons of Noah, after their generations, in their nations: and by these were the nations divided in the earth after the flood."

Gen 10:5 — "By these were the isles of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations."

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

Deu 32:8 — "When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The age would either deny the common descent of all peoples or weaponize ancestry into racial division; the Table of Nations teaches one blood under one God, ordered for the gathering of all nations into Christ.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The matter to weigh is the unity and ordering of mankind. Against every racialism that would set the peoples at enmity by blood, the Table of Nations declares that God hath made of one blood all nations of men; there is no master-race and no devil-race, for all descend from Noah and from Adam. And against the modern denial of any God-given order to the nations, Scripture teaches that the Most High Himself divided the inheritance and set the bounds of the peoples—the rise and place of nations is no accident but the appointment of providence. The Babel scattering that follows is judgment on pride, not the abolition of the nations God had ordered.

The principle to recover is one blood under one God, gathered into one people in Christ. The diversity of nations and tongues is God’s ordering, not a curse to be erased; yet the division of Babel is healed not by a new tower of human unity but at Pentecost and in the gospel, where men of every nation, kindred, tongue, and people are redeemed by one blood—the blood of Christ—into one new man. The Table of Nations begins the story that ends with a multitude out of every nation before the throne.
